outcomes.text: Find the main clause and the complete spans of its embedded clauses.
Read C and S under S′ with “that”, unfilled C or interrogative “whether”.
Use the clause’s function and host to decide where it attaches.

opening.prompt: In “Mina says that the gate jammed”, which group gives the complete content of her report?

options.feedback: This introduces the report. The content follows “says”.
This span includes the introductory word and the reported event.
That is only the subject inside the report.

opening.prompt: In “Ari wondered whether the hall was open”, which word introduces the embedded question?

options.feedback: “Whether” introduces the question about the hall.
This is the verb in the main clause.
This verb belongs in the embedded predicate.

opening.prompt: In “That the lights went out surprised Ren”, what surprised Ren?

options.feedback: Ren is the person who was surprised.
This identifies the subject inside the embedded clause.
The whole clause tells what caused the surprise.

opening.prompt: What does “that the ferry was late” supply in “the claim that the ferry was late”?

options.feedback: The clause states what someone claimed.
The clause completes the noun “claim”.
The clause does not identify the person making it.

opening.prompt: In “The crew stopped because the rope snapped”, which group gives the reason for stopping?

options.feedback: The full reason clause includes “because”.
This is the subject inside the reason clause.
This names the event that the reason explains.

closing.prompt: In “Ren thinks Ivo knows the bell rang”, which is the most deeply embedded clause?

options.text: Ren thinks Ivo knows the bell rang
options.feedback: This is the main clause, including both embedded clauses.
This clause is embedded under “thinks”, and it contains a further clause.
This clause supplies what Ivo knows, inside what Ren thinks.

closing.prompt: In “Ria heard the ferry had left”, what word appears under C in the embedded clause tree?

options.feedback: “That” could be supplied in a different version. It is absent here.
C is unfilled. The inner S begins at “the ferry”.
“Had” is inside the embedded predicate.

closing.prompt: In “Ivo asked whether the door was locked”, what is the word order inside the embedded S?

options.feedback: “Whether” occupies C. The subject comes before “was” inside S.
This is the order of the standalone yes/no question.
This is the whole S′. The inner S begins after “whether”.

closing.prompt: In “It bothered Nia that the lamp flickered”, where does the extraposed S′ attach in this analysis?

options.feedback: Dummy “it” fills the subject slot in this version.

options.text: Beside the verb inside the main VP
options.feedback: The final clause supplies what bothered Nia. It is the extraposed subject.
The extraposed clause attaches beside the subject NP and the predicate VP.

closing.prompt: In “Ren stayed after the rain stopped”, what does temporal “after” take as its complement?

options.feedback: The complement includes the predicate “stopped” as well.
The preposition “after” and the bare S form a PP in this analysis.
“After” heads the PP. It is outside the clause that it takes as complement.
